original_question: For each dimension s >= 2 and positive integer q, let D(a_1, ..., a_s; q) be the discrepancy of the multidimensional Korobov-Hlawka sequence defined in the paper. Is the true order of min_{(a_1,...,a_s) in Z^s} D(a_1, ..., a_s; q) bounded by O_s((log q)^(s-1))? Equivalently, can the extra factor log log q in Bykovskii's bound O_s((log q)^(s-1) log log q) be removed?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the survey's later Zaremba/good-lattice-points discussion that asks whether the known upper bound for the minimum discrepancy of Korobov-Hlawka lattice point sets can be improved by deleting the extra factor log log q from Bykovskii's estimate.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical target very well: it asks about the minimum discrepancy of s-dimensional Korobov-Hlawka point sets, fixes the dimension s and modulus q, and focuses on the specific sharpening suggested by the paper's discussion of Bykovskii's bound, namely whether the extra factor log log q is artefactual. That is the right problem, and it stays narrowly aligned with the paper's intent rather than drifting to a broader discrepancy question.
missing_details: The object should be defined explicitly as a finite Korobov-Hlawka point set/grid K_q(a_1,...,a_s) = {({a_1 k/q},...,{a_s k/q}) : k = 1,...,q} in [0,1)^s; calling it a 'sequence' is slightly ambiguous in this context.
The discrepancy must be defined stand-alone, i.e. as the supremum over axis-parallel half-open boxes in [0,1)^s.

The normalization should be fixed explicitly. In the standard discrepancy notation one has disc(K_q(a)) <<_s (log q)^{s-1} log log q / q, whereas your draft uses the rescaled quantity without the factor 1/q.
The minimization domain should be specified: only the residue classes modulo q matter, and one usually imposes gcd(a_1,...,a_s,q) = 1 so that the point set has q distinct nodes.
The asymptotic quantifier should be explicit: the question is for each fixed s as q -> infinity, with the implied constant depending only on s.

It helps to say that this is the multidimensional extension of the classical good-lattice-point/Zaremba-type problem, especially because the case s = 2 is the classical boundary case in the surrounding literature.

If one wants the question to be fully faithful to the literature cited around the paper, one should distinguish the usual discrepancy disc(K_q(a)) from the rescaled minimum discrepancy quantity q * disc(K_q(a)).
refined_question: For fixed s >= 2 and q >= 2, and for a = (a_1,...,a_s) in Z^s with gcd(a_1,...,a_s,q) = 1, let K_q(a) = {({a_1 k/q},...,{a_s k/q}) : k = 1,...,q} subset [0,1)^s be the s-dimensional Korobov-Hlawka point set. Let disc(K_q(a)) denote its discrepancy from the uniform distribution with respect to axis-parallel half-open boxes, and set Delta_q(a) := q * disc(K_q(a)). Is it true that for every fixed dimension s one has min_a Delta_q(a) <<_s (log q)^(s-1) as q -> infinity? In other words, can one remove the extra factor log log q from the best known general upper bound min_a Delta_q(a) <<_s (log q)^(s-1) log log q?
justification: The draft is substantively on target: it singles out exactly the sharpening that the survey points to in the Korobov-Hlawka/good-lattice discussion, namely the removal of the log log q loss from Bykovskii's upper bound. What needed sharpening was not the mathematical aim but the stand-alone formulation: the paper's underlying object is a finite point set K_q(a), the discrepancy needs to be defined explicitly, and the normalization has to be fixed because the literature alternates between disc(K_q(a)) and the rescaled quantity q * disc(K_q(a)). The nearest official formulation in the survey appears to be unnumbered rather than a formal conjecture. The precise asymptotic form of the known bound and the statement that only a factor log log N separates it from the conjectured order are stated explicitly in Bykovskii's 2012 paper, which is the source the survey is invoking. A later paper of Illarionov restates the same Korobov-Hlawka notation cleanly and confirms the same discrepancy normalization.
